column58: Developing firmware for a brushless DC motor controller used in a small appliance.
column59: The existing controller had audible noise at low speed, so the team investigated the PWM switching strategy.

column62: Audible noise dropped noticeably and the revised firmware was carried into the next hardware revision.

column69: Manual testing took too long and results were inconsistent between operators.

column79: I designed and simulated the MPPT algorithm and built the control board.
column80: The first algorithm converged too slowly under fast-changing light. I switched to an incremental-conductance method and retuned it.
column81: Efficiency improved by about 14% over the baseline under partial shading, measured on the physical prototype.

column69: The site had variable soil conditions across the span, and the design needed reliable bearing capacity data.

column77: Final year project evaluating whether an existing RC frame building meets current seismic code requirements.
column78: The building was designed under an older code and its actual seismic performance was unknown.
column79: I built the ETABS model, ran the pushover analysis, and identified the weak storey.
column80: The initial model did not match the as-built drawings in a few bays. I revisited the site survey and corrected the model before rerunning the analysis.
column81: The study confirmed a soft-storey irregularity at the ground floor and proposed a jacketing retrofit that met the target performance level.
